payload: {"schema":1,"version":"0.0.55","date":"2026-11-01","lede":"Faster, lighter clay: sculpting up to 5x faster on half the memory; a Primitives tool with 133 parametric shapes for Poly and Clay; Color correct looks in the Library; Smooth or Handles curves with a live dab preview; Sharp retopology hits its polycount with clean open borders","highlights":["Faster, lighter clay","Primitives tool","Point instancing in instance packs","Clay layer resolution","Color correct looks","More ways to blend clay"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.55","windows":{"url":"https://github.com/c6ank/klay-releases/releases/download/0.0.55/Klay_Setup_0.0.55.exe","size":409394438,"sha512":"4667b2636493a20cf186f31d02066871a75374de0145538f50be99196d0fd998cbec59bbd7b22895c4987f778541bc82b4af9c8bcd79d3b054a49032e3bf6b13"},"mac":{"version":"0.0.55","url":"https://github.com/c6ank/klay-releases/releases/download/0.0.55/Klay_0.0.55_macOS.dmg","size":612252780,"sha512":"ded1e03878b4efce0508d4876bd5c5e8ab3a4c45005c0951866d2c9f0ca61c047d8bf06da8acac24d70456bcb7412a5335fe173bb1d20617b19ac1ec0c1ed27b"},"items":[{"g":"n","t":"Faster, lighter clay","b":"Clay sculpting is up to four to five times faster and a clay object uses about half the video memory, so larger and more detailed clay fits on the same card. Large strokes now release without a pause.","w":["Clay layers"]},{"g":"n","t":"Primitives tool","b":"A new Primitives tool places parametric shapes from a library of 133 primitives in fourteen families, from boxes and polyhedra to gears, knots, lattices, fractals and text, with families for nature (rock, crystals, tree stump, water drop, cloud), hard surface parts (beams, pipe fittings, flanges, screws, hinges, knobs, sprockets, grilles), architecture (roofs, domes, window and door frames, stairs, vaults, brick walls, cobblestones), patterns and surfaces, and mathematical art. Each shape can be made as a poly mesh or as clay. A switch at the top of the card adds two more modes: Box shapes a cube by extruding, insetting, loop-cutting and rounding its edges, each action available as a tile with its shortcut; Lasso turns a closed outline drawn in the viewport into a rounded shape, with five height curves, puffed dots and ridges drawn inside it. Click places a shape on the surface under the cursor and dragging sets its size. The tool card edits the shape's own parameters together with shared deform, repeat, symmetry, edge, surface and boolean settings, and can morph one shape into another. The Surface section offers 22 noises, among them Voronoi, Crackle, Marble, Wood grain, Scales, Rust and Drips, and six more patterns (Honeycomb, Bricks, Studs, Craters, Shatter and Basket weave); a Noise advanced section holds their fractal, cell, warp, shape and break-up settings. Handles on the shape resize it and adjust its parameters, an arrow past each size handle moves it along that axis, and dragging the ring around the centre dot scales the whole shape evenly. Shift+A opens a searchable picker that lists each shape by its icon and name, grouped by family; in the Library each primitive is shown by the same icon, with its rendered preview on hover. Favourites appear under Quick add and in the Library, and a right-click on a primitive offers Swap shape, Randomize, Copy and Paste parameters, Bake and Convert between Poly and Clay. The picker's pin button keeps it open after a pick, so it can be moved by its header and its Swap shape applies to whichever primitive is selected next. The shapes of a clay layer are listed under it in the outliner, each with an icon of its own shape (a shape that cuts shows it dashed), as are primitives placed as poly meshes: a click selects one for the gizmo, Ctrl and Shift select several, and dragging rows changes the order in which the shapes combine, moves them into or out of a group, or moves them to another clay layer at the drop position. The gizmo on selected shapes has every control of the Gizmo tool, including the pivot buttons, and its scale handles resize the shapes. Duplicate, from Ctrl+D or the row menu, copies the selected shapes inside the same layer, and scaling the layer scales its shapes with it. Each row shows how its shape joins the ones above it, with the operations and blends of the Boolean panel (Round, Chamfer, Muscle, Groove, Weld and Inflate); click it to edit the join, or drag it sideways to change the blend width. Shapes can be grouped, from the row menu or the outliner's Group button, so that a group combines on its own before it joins the rest of the layer. With symmetry on, a placed shape gets a linked mirror that follows every change to its parameters, blend and shape, can be moved, rotated or scaled from either side, and on clay can be unlinked from its outliner row. Handles on mirror, in the card's Handles section, shows the handles on the mirror as well, so a shape can be adjusted from either side. Moving or editing one shape on a clay layer rebuilds only the area around it, so it stays responsive on layers that hold many shapes or groups.","w":["Tools \u203a Primitives"]},{"g":"n","t":"Point instancing in instance packs","b":"An instance pack holds copies of one or more objects as points, far beyond the previous limit of about a thousand copies per scene, and draws them faster than the same number of separate copies. Instance point adds the selection as a point to the current pack, or creates a pack when there is none; move the new point and press it again within five seconds to repeat the move. Create > Instance pack makes an empty pack and Add to pack chooses the target pack, the outliner lists each object of a pack with its own visibility, and a single point can be selected, moved, duplicated or removed. Packs work with poly and clay objects, shadows and the path tracer, and Ctrl+D still makes a separate copy.","w":["Right-click \u203a Copy \u203a Instance point"]},{"g":"n","t":"Clay layer resolution","b":"Each clay layer has a resolution of Low, Default, High, Ultra or Extreme, chosen from the capsule beside its name in the outliner, which also shows the layer's scale in its colour. Clay layers now also show a rendered thumbnail on their outliner card, like poly meshes, refreshed when you switch to another layer. A higher resolution gives a bigger box at the same detail; Extreme is meant for graphics cards with plenty of memory, a lower one cuts the clay outside the smaller box after asking first, and Undo restores it.","w":["Outliner \u203a Clay layer \u203a Resolution"]},{"g":"n","t":"Color correct looks","b":"The Library has a Color correct category of saved looks, each shown on the same grey sphere so they compare side by side. Click a look to apply it to the Post process; turn off Click applies to select with a click and apply with a double-click. Every Color correct panel (Post, the Camera Grade panel and the picture viewer) now has Copy, Paste and Save at the top, and shows the name of the look last applied.","w":["Library \u203a Color correct"]},{"g":"n","t":"More ways to blend clay","b":"The clay Boolean panel's Blending section adds Inset, Extrude, Line groove, Tongue, Repel and Avoid, which press, raise or engrave one object into another or make the objects give way to each other. A folded More blends section holds twelve further joins: Columns, Stairs, Pipe and Split edge for hard surfaces, Noisy, Sag, Stretch and Bridge for organic joins, and Exclude, Morph, Shell and Replace. A Type switch under the tiles sets how every join is rounded: Smooth, Chamfer, or, from the \u22ef button, Soft, Circular, Silky and Exact. The same joins and types are available on the shapes of a clay layer made with the Primitives tool, from the outliner's Join card, whose Blending section can be folded to keep only the Union, Subtract and Intersect switch, and from the right-click Join menu.","w":["Boolean \u203a Clay \u203a Blending"]},{"g":"n","t":"Zen toolbar","b":"A compact, icon-only bottom toolbar: the round dot at the right end of the toolbar switches to it, the short bar at its right end switches back, and Ctrl+T (Cmd+T on macOS) switches between the two. Names and shortcuts appear on hover, and the brush drawer and the tools list open above it. Drag either arrow sideways to show more or fewer brushes or tools; hold a brush or a tool to drag it to a new place, as on the full toolbar. The full toolbar's brush arrow, and a new arrow on its Tools card, resize the same way.","w":["Bottom toolbar \u203a Zen toolbar"]},{"g":"n","t":"Brush pastille","b":"An optional column on the left of the viewport for the Zen toolbar, turned on by right-clicking the toolbar: Radius and Strength sit at the top, followed by any functions, brush settings, Stamp, Falloff, Stencil, dividers, switches and folders you add with Add function. Right-click the pastille to add, reorder or remove items.","w":["Zen toolbar \u203a right-click \u203a Brush pastille"]},{"g":"n","t":"Folds growth for stamp brushes","b":"The stamp brush's Growth section has a Branches | Folds switch. With Folds, holding the brush on a clay layer grows a folded, organic surface from a small ball or from the clay under the brush. The clay itself changes smoothly at frame rate while you hold, at a steady pace that does not depend on the frame rate (about seven seconds to the Stop at size), with folds kept thick enough that the surface stays closed, and releasing it keeps the result as one undo step; Esc during the hold restores the clay. Grown from the clay under the brush, the folds become the clay's own surface, with no second surface left underneath, so they can also turn inward into the clay; grown from a ball, the growth is added onto the clay. Dragging the brush seeds new growth along the whole stroke, anywhere on the layer, at the brush's spacing. The new Frill, Lettuce, Coral, Fine coral, Brain and Swell stamp brushes are set up for it. Settle after freezes older growth away from the growing edges so it no longer counts toward Max points, which lets the edges keep growing during long holds.","w":["Brush \u203a Growth \u203a Folds"]},{"g":"n","t":"Volume texture for clay brushes","b":"Any clay brush can project a grayscale image through the clay with triplanar mapping, on top of what the brush already does. Strength sets how much it acts. Add raises the light parts and sinks the dark ones, Carve only digs the dark parts in, and Break cuts the brush's own deposit where the image is dark, so the stroke lands as broken chunks. Map, Triplanar and Cells offer the same controls as the Flood tab's Displace texture.","w":["Brush \u203a Noise & patterns \u203a Volume texture"]},{"g":"n","t":"Crease and rake in clay","b":"The clay Elastique brush can now crease and rake clay live: drag across the surface to fold the clay ahead of the brush and leave a clean groove behind it, from a soft valley to a knife-sharp crease or a raised ridge. The groove's profile, depth and width respond to pen pressure, and Slide warp lets the surface stretch and bunch around it like skin. Holding Ctrl, or turning on Invert brush, raises the same profile out of the surface instead of cutting it. Dab length sets how often the groove is laid down, so a shorter step follows quick turns closely.","w":["Brush \u203a Elastique \u203a Surface slide"]},{"g":"n","t":"Poly brushes in the Clay tab","b":"Right-click a brush in the toolbar's Poly tab and choose Copy to Clay preset to add a copy of it to the Clay tab, where it sculpts clay layers with the same behaviour. The copy is a separate preset: changing its settings does not affect the original brush.","w":["Toolbar \u203a Poly \u203a right-click \u203a Copy to Clay preset"]},{"g":"n","t":"Smooth or Handles curves","b":"Every curve editor has a Smooth | Handles switch under the graph. Smooth keeps the current behaviour. Handles draws B\u00e9zier segments whose handles follow the points automatically; drag a handle to bend that point by hand, and right-click the handle to make it automatic again. Points and handles highlight under the cursor. The mode and any bent handles are saved with each curve. The area under the curve is now filled, and the brush Falloff curve shows a live preview of the dab above it that updates while you drag a point.","w":["Brush \u203a Falloff curve"]},{"g":"f","t":"The gizmo now scales a clay layer evenly on all three axes. Scaling a clay layer along one axis, which distorted the clay, is no longer offered."},{"g":"f","t":"The installer no longer refuses to install when an earlier Klay was removed by deleting its folder. It now clears the leftover entry and continues, and if an earlier version cannot be uninstalled it offers to install over it."},{"g":"f","t":"In VR through Virtual Desktop, the headset image no longer looks darker than the viewport. If another VR runtime shows the headset too dark or too bright, the VR window's Headset output setting changes how the image is handed to it."},{"g":"f","t":"A Laser cut with fill through parts that pass into each other, such as fingers resting on a palm, crossing strands or an unmerged sculpt, now fills each part cleanly. The fill previously could leave holes or flipped faces at the seam. These cuts are also faster."},{"g":"f","t":"After many Move strokes on a clay object, patches of the surface no longer disappear where you pulled. They previously stayed missing until a Smooth stroke passed over them."},{"g":"f","t":"The clay Elastique brush now shows its Compressibility while you drag, so the surface no longer shifts slightly when you release."},{"g":"f","t":"With symmetry on, the dot that marks the mirrored brush position is now hidden when it is behind the model."},{"g":"f","t":"The Mirror tool's cut keeps quads where the mirror plane crosses a row of quads. The centre seam previously became a strip of triangles."},{"g":"f","t":"Sharp retopology now produces close to the polycount you set. It previously gave about a third of the target on the starter head (around 1,900 faces for 5,000)."},{"g":"f","t":"After a gizmo Align, scaling along one axis no longer distorts the model and no longer makes the gizmo disappear. Align now turns the green axis to the picked face."},{"g":"f","t":"Undoing or redoing a gizmo move, rotation or scale now brings the gizmo back with the object. It previously stayed where the drag had ended."},{"g":"f","t":"Selecting with V now works on clay objects the same way as on poly: a drag box selects every clay object it covers, a single one becomes the active layer, and a V click no longer creates a new clay layer."},{"g":"f","t":"After a Boolean between a clay object and a poly mesh, deleting another clay object no longer leaves a copy of the used clay object in the viewport that could not be selected in the outliner or deleted. Undo now also restores that clay object correctly."},{"g":"f","t":"Redo after undoing a Laser cut on a clay object now restores the cut exactly. It could previously bring back a damaged surface."},{"g":"f","t":"Voxelize now shows only the finished result, with its detail projected. The bare voxel shell no longer appears for a moment before the detail."},{"g":"f","t":"Favourites in the library are no longer limited: pinning a new one no longer removes the oldest. Clicking the Stamp or Falloff tile on the toolbar shows every favourite in a grid."},{"g":"f","t":"On a narrow Library window the header buttons no longer run under the Size slider: Import, Save current, Click applies and Re-render all now sit on their own row under the header, with Size at its right."},{"g":"f","t":"The Library button in the top bar now reopens the Library on the category you last used, including after a restart. It previously always opened on Clay stamps."},{"g":"f","t":"Video memory is released after you subdivide a mesh to a high level. About 1 GB used to stay reserved for the rest of the session, even after a new scene or with only a small model left."},{"g":"f","t":"Boolean and Blend results on clay objects now keep each object's surface smooth. The preview and the applied result could previously show blocky bumps over the whole surface, away from the join."},{"g":"f","t":"With symmetry on, clay brushes with Elastique or Surface slide now warp both sides as mirror images and no longer drag clay across the symmetry plane."}],"history":[{"version":"0.0.54","date":"2026-10-26","lede":"Studio licence server, compact right-click menu with your own quick actions, timer-dial undo strip","highlights":["Studio licence server","Edit placement and Recenter for clay objects"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.54","items":[{"g":"n","t":"Studio licence server","b":"A studio can share a pool of seats across its network from one licence server. Each workstation takes a seat while Klay is open and returns it when Klay closes; when no seat is free, the panel lists who holds them.","w":["Settings \u203a Licence \u203a Studio server"]},{"g":"n","t":"Edit placement and Recenter for clay objects","b":"Edit placement shows a box around the clay volume. Move, rotate and resize it with the gizmo, the corner handles and the arrows on its edges, then Apply: the clay stays in place and is resampled into the box, finer when the box is smaller. Recenter object moves the sculpt to the middle of its volume without moving it in the scene.","w":["Right-click a clay object \u203a Edit placement"]},{"g":"n","t":"Live preview in Projection","b":"With Live preview on, the transfer is shown on the target before you press Project and updates when a setting or the source changes. Paint a mask on the target to hold areas back; the preview updates when the stroke ends. Project keeps the result, Cancel removes it.","w":["Right-click a mesh \u203a Projection \u203a Live preview"],"k":["[P]"]},{"g":"i","t":"A compact right-click menu","b":"The object menu now shows one row per category, with the verbs of each in a side menu, so it fits on screen. A row of quick actions sits at the top: right-click one to choose the function it holds, from this menu or from the app functions of the sidebar rail. Create gathers everything you can add, sculpt layers included, and Export gains Export all.","w":["Right-click an object"]},{"g":"i","t":"Undo strip reads like a dial","b":"The quick undo strip is now a sliding scale of step marks with numbers, the current step lit in the highlight colour. It keeps the same spacing at any history length; drag, flick, click a mark or use the wheel.","w":["Settings \u203a Undo \u203a Quick undo strip"],"k":["[Ctrl Z]"]},{"g":"i","t":"Brush value drag can be rebound","b":"The right-drag that sets brush size and strength is now a shortcut. It can take a modifier or a key on the right button, or be turned off.","w":["Settings \u203a Shortcuts \u203a Tools \u203a Brush value drag"]},{"g":"i","t":"Reduce a clay object from the menu","b":"Reduce, the opposite of Subdivide, now sits next to it in the clay object menu and makes the clay coarser.
